overview: Candidates generally attempted all MCQs, handled standard form well, chose equations correctly from the data booklet and structured solutions clearly.
Do not truncate or round mid-calculation; keep full calculator values.
Use precise vocabulary - oscillation, superposition, interference, work function, resolution, (directly) proportional - to communicate physics succinctly.
Momentum is a vector: reversals of direction must be included when finding change in momentum.
Convert to SI units (e.g. mm to m) before substituting to avoid power of ten errors.
Photoelectric explanations and practical-technique language (random error, resolution, parallax) were notable weaknesses.
assessment_for_learning: Percentage difference = (measured - accepted)/accepted x 100%; see the Practical Skills Handbook.
Use the Practical Skills Handbook for definitions of practical terms and techniques.
Frequency does not change when a wave enters a new medium; v is proportional to wavelength.
When a question refers to data in a figure, use or manipulate that data in the answer.

common_errors: Repeated readings without measuring the diameter at different places along the wire

common_errors: Confused E (Young modulus) with energy and used E = 1/2 Fx or 1/2 kx^2

common_errors: Gave a qualitative comparison
Only calculated the difference between values
Divided the difference by the calculated value instead of the accepted value
good_practice: Made a quantitative comparison (percentage difference vs percentage uncertainty)

common_errors: Weak descriptions of molecule motion lacking 'oscillate' and 'parallel'
good_practice: Explained compressions and rarefactions in terms of molecule spacing

common_errors: Confused descriptions of nodes and antinodes
good_practice: Superposition of incident and reflected waves; antinodes from constructive and nodes from destructive interference

common_errors: Attributed the change to frequency or phase changes

good_practice: Reflected wave's amplitude/intensity decreases with distance from sheet A, so nodes are less complete further away

common_errors: Suggested repeats without averaging
good_practice: Measure across many nodes, or lower the frequency to lengthen the wavelength and reduce percentage uncertainty

common_errors: Linked energy to frequency without mentioning photons
good_practice: Each photon must have energy at least equal to the work function, the minimum energy to release an electron

common_errors: Said greater intensity gives more photoelectrons without linking to rate of photons
Reversed the causality
Referred to the ammeter reading rather than current
misconceptions: Not applying the one-to-one photon-electron interaction

common_errors: Used P = VI with the 3 V battery and Q = It to find power
misconceptions: Not recognising that photon energy delivered per second is the power
good_practice: Power = photon rate x hf, then I = P/A
